set_aside.subject: recovery precedence for operation-element state
set_aside.text: “an element whose approval the owner approved … is not reached and so is ready” and “a conclusion … is taken as it is”
set_aside.question: When an element has both an approved unused approval and a concluded NodeExecution—for example, an approved send whose pre-send check wrote `operation_failed`—which fact controls recovery?
options: The concluded NodeExecution wins and the element is never reached again
The approved approval makes the element ready and it is reached again
Define an explicit precedence over waits, resolutions, conclusions and approvals
set_aside.default_guess: The concluded NodeExecution wins, except that an EffectAttempt resolved `not_applied` explicitly overrides its `outcome_unknown` NodeExecution and makes the element ready.

set_aside.subject: draft trace records discovered while recovering a waiting run
set_aside.text: “A run derived still waiting has only its lagging status and waiting points rewritten.”
set_aside.question: What happens to `skipped_by_guard` and `upstream_failed` drafts that `run_graph.plan_run` derives for a run that also still has waiting elements?
options: `runs` writes the drafts before writing the waiting status and points
The drafts are deliberately deferred until a later request or recovery
A waiting derivation is guaranteed never to contain drafts
set_aside.default_guess: `runs` writes all newly determined drafts in their required order, then writes the derived status and waiting points.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: sandbox runner report decoding
set_aside.text: “`sandbox_runner` owns … the reading of the report it sent to the parent” while “`sandbox` owns … every judgement from outside”
set_aside.question: What outcome does `sandbox` report when `read_runner_report` receives no complete report, invalid framing, malformed fields or an oversized report from a runner process that otherwise exits normally?
options: Treat it as an internal kernel error and stop the kernel
Give each report failure a stated mapping
set_aside.default_guess: Classify an invalid or incomplete runner report as `crashed`, subject to the existing timeout and resource-exhaustion precedence.
